aliases: It's Completely Fine: The Toynbee Project
films.title: It's Completely Fine: The Toynbee Project
films.description: Traffic Skateboards' sixth full-length turns 20 years of East Coast spot seeking into a 27-minute team film. Jake Todd filmed the project and co-edited it with Pat Stiener, building seven principal chapters around a broad Traffic roster and a Toynbee-tile visual motif.
creditNotes: The authorized complete-film description identifies Traffic's sixth full-length, chapters Kevin Coakley, the shared montage, Hiroki Muraoka, Chris Teta, Luke Malaney, Josh Feist and James Sayres, and credits Jake Todd with filming plus Todd and Pat Stiener with editing.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies the project as a 27-minute 2024 Traffic full-length by Jake Todd, catalogs 16 appearances and documents the soundtrack chapter structure.

Josh Wilhite and Justin Grzechowiak are retained as explicitly named shared-montage riders in the first-party description and independently documented soundtrack section rather than being promoted to solo-part status.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite identifies the film's Philadelphia context, while TransWorld describes the team as an East Coast spot-seeking crew and specifically notes Kevin Coakley's Massachusetts terrain.
films.historicalContext: Released during Traffic Skateboards' twentieth year, the film extends the brand's blue-collar East Coast lineage and uses handmade Toynbee-inspired tiles as its recurring identity. Village Psychic's contemporary interview with Pat Stiener and Jake Todd documents the multi-year production and tile-making process.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is a dedicated skate still with the film title and no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: MOMENTUM
films.description: Madrid Skateboards' 21-minute team full-length moves through eleven riders in a precisely chaptered order of appearance. The company's official release spans veteran Lester Kasai, a returning Mike Berdis, Daniel Yeager and a new generation of Madrid riders before Phil Ceja's two-song closer.
creditNotes: Madrid Skateboards' official upload publishes all eleven riders in order of appearance and separates repeated Mike Berdis passages and Phil Ceja's two-song closing section.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies MOMENTUM as a 21-minute 2024 Madrid full-length, identifies Daniel Yeager as filmmaker, corroborates all eleven riders and records twenty additional production contributors.
The additional contributors are retained under SkateVideoSite's generic production-credit label; more specific formal roles are not inferred.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite identifies the production country as the United States. Madrid's first-party premiere notice documents the film's debut at OC Ramps in Santa Ana, California, but that premiere venue is not treated as a filming location.
films.historicalContext: Madrid premiered MOMENTUM at OC Ramps on July 20, 2024 and released it through the company's own channel the following day, adding a modern team full-length to a skateboard manufacturer whose history reaches back to 1976.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is dedicated Madrid-branded film artwork with the MOMENTUM title, a fisheye skate image and no trailer or episode labeling.

Madrid's first-party site announces the July 20 OC Ramps premiere of its new full-length MOMENTUM and directs nonlocal viewers to the official YouTube release.

Video de Deza Skateboards NADA ES PARA SIEMPRE
films.title: Nada Es Para Siempre
films.description: Deza Skateboards' first full-length follows an eight-rider international team across Mexico, the United States and Europe for 36 minutes. Pepe Baeza filmed and edited the project, while owner Shadi Charbel shaped its skits and a title concept about accepting that nothing lasts forever.
films.releaseNote: TransWorld published the complete film and its first-party interview on December 29, 2024. Deza's own YouTube copy was uploaded January 7, 2025; the canonical 2024 year follows the film's documented release and independent cataloging rather than the later official-channel mirror date.
additionalProductionCredits: Jesus Guerrero (production credit and skit concept)
creditNotes: Deza Skateboards' official complete-film description thanks the riders and production contributors, while the exact roster is cross-checked against SkateVideoSite's eight documented skaters.

TransWorld's contemporary interview with Deza owner Shadi Charbel identifies this as the company's only full-length, explains the title and skit concepts, and formally credits Pepe Baeza with filming and editing.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the film as a 36-minute 2024 Deza full-length by Pepe Baeza and preserves the additional editor, animation, color, production and filmer/photographer credits. Generic credit labels are retained without inventing narrower roles.
films.locationNote: TransWorld documents that most of the film was shot across Mexico, Richard Moore's part was filmed entirely in the United States, Danny Ruiz's section was filmed in El Paso, and Flo Marfaing's European footage was shot mostly in Spain.
films.historicalContext: Filming began during the 2020 pandemic and grew into Deza Skateboards' first full-length. Shadi Charbel tied the title to accepting the end of his own skating ambitions after knee surgeries, while the film's international structure connects Deza's Mexican base to riders in the United States and Europe.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is a dedicated black-and-white title card carrying the Deza logo and the English subtitle 'Nothing Is Forever,' with no trailer or episode labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Deza Skateboards' official channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and names its riders and contributors. YouTube reports channelId UC0WtDDRLim7aqtyDQMVPHOw, a 2,207-second main feature, January 7, 2025 upload and embed permission.

Contemporary December 29, 2024 coverage embeds the complete film and publishes a detailed first-party interview with Deza owner Shadi Charbel covering its release, filming history, locations, team structure, title and Pepe Baeza's filming/editing credit.
Independent filmography classifies Nada Es Para Siempre as a 36-minute 2024 Deza full-length by Pepe Baeza, corroborates all eight skaters and catalogs the available production contributors.
